assumptions.assumption: Public CelesTrak / 18 SDS GP element sets update frequently enough on watched objects to distinguish discrete thruster burns from secular perturbation drift.
assumptions.test: Flag any watched object whose TLE gap exceeds 48 hours (OR-IND-4) and cap maneuver confidence at Low when a gap spans the detection window.
assumptions.note: Manoeuvre lane live from orbit-2.4 on Space-Track element sets, with no confidence (a change is listed or not; doctrine/method.md). Gaps of 48 hours or more are labelled on each change. Known cases (docs/validation/maneuver-calibration.md): the ISS had a set every 3 hours at the median, the GEO cases every 9-14 hours, and the known burns there stand well clear of the drift; live gaps have reached 37 days (Luch (Olymp) 2, 15 Oct to 22 Nov 2026).

assumptions.assumption: GCAT's State column keeps Soviet (SU) objects apart from Russian Federation (RU) objects, where CelesTrak's owner code merges them as CIS.
assumptions.test: Count SU and RU in each reading (hygiene block). Read 13 Nov 2026: 16,148 SU and 9,183 RU in satcat.

assumptions.assumption: GCAT catalogs payloads from a new launch within days, so 'not yet cataloged' on a launch item is a lag, not an absence.
assumptions.test: Track days from launch to first payload entry across readings; 13 Nov 2026 the four Tanluzhe objects of 11 Nov were in tmpcat two days after launch.

assumptions.assumption: A Launch Library 2 schedule entry reflects the provider's or press's public schedule; dates move and some launches (notably Chinese and Russian military) are listed late or not at all.
